Tessa — quick legal read after looking at SDK_DPA_redlines_20261124.pdf. High-level:
- Retention (1 year): Prefer 3 years as standard. However, we can consent to 1 year if: 1) customer accepts a higher per-GB fee or 2) we add a narrow exception for backup/forensic copies (standard ephemeral backups not held beyond 90 days). Recommend we propose a compromise: 18 months, with an option to shorten to 12 months in writing for regulated data types.
- Data residency (US/EU): Acceptable operationally if they sign Appendix A (region-limited) and agree to a migration window for any future region request. Security to confirm technical constraints.
- Subprocessors (30-day notice): 30 days is tight but manageable. Ask for a notification + objection window of 30 days and a defined remedy if they object (i.e., migration or termination for that processing only).
- HIPAA language: We should not convert the DPA into a full BAA; instead offer a HIPAA Addendum that maps security controls but routes signature to Legal/Compliance. That will require an exec-level sign-off for HIPAA support.

Next steps from legal: I'll prepare a redline accepting data residency and subprocessors with the proposed guardrails. Retention counter-proposal: 18 months (commercial concession). For HIPAA we prepare an addendum template and mark as 'requires exec approval'.

Marcus
Marcus Lin | Senior Counsel, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the patience. We've reviewed SDK's redlines and can move forward with a small set of concessions and a clear routing plan:

Accepted / proposed:
- Data residency: Agree to restrict processing to US and EU regions. We'll include an Appendix A and a 30-day migration window for any future region requests.
- Subprocessors: We'll accept a 30-day notice + 30-day objection window. If SDK objects to a new subprocessor, we'll work with you on mitigation or scoped termination for the impacted processing.
- Retention: Counter-proposal of 18 months standard. If you require 12 months for specific regulated datasets, we can evaluate as a written exception with a commercial adjustment (see below).

HIPAA / PHI: We are not adding full BAA language into the DPA. We will provide a HIPAA Addendum template that requires VP-level approval and signing. If SDK intends to send PHI in production, we'll need to execute that addendum and scope the SOW accordingly.

Commercial concession: As discussed internally, Redwood will provide a one-time 10% onboarding credit contingent on SDK accepting the 18-month retention term and the standard subprocessors clause.

Next steps / signature path:
1) Legal (Marcus) will send a redlined DPA accepting the above by EOD tomorrow.
2) If SDK agrees, we'll send a DocuSign envelope for the DPA (and separate DocuSign for HIPAA Addendum if needed).
3) For HIPAA addendum execution we will require VP/CRO signature; we will flag that early if SDK proceeds.

DocuSign link (will be activated with final redlines): https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/1234-ABCD

Please confirm acceptance of the 18-month retention compromise and the onboarding credit, or advise if you need different commercial terms. We aim to have signatures in place before your Dec 7 board meeting.
